result.instructions: Tools for Status.io, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Are there any active incidents on my status page right now?"; "Which components are on my status page and what is their status?"; "Show past incidents that were resolved recently.". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Status.io data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run statusio_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run statusio_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run statusio_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. statusio_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: statusio_get_status_summary
tools.title: Get status summary
tools.description: The current state of the status page in one call: overall status, every component and container with its status code and last update, open incidents and active/upcoming maintenance. Start here. GET /status/summary/{statuspage_id}.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

tools.name: statusio_list_components
tools.title: List components
tools.description: List the components of the status page and the containers (data centers / locations) attached to each, with ids. Component and container ids are needed to update a status or to say what an incident affects ('<component_id>-<container_id>'). GET /component/list/{statuspage_id}.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

tools.name: statusio_list_incidents
tools.title: List incident ids
tools.description: The ids of all active and resolved incidents (ids only, no details): a quick way to see which incidents exist. Fetch one with statusio_get_incident. GET /incidents/{statuspage_id}.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

tools.name: statusio_list_active_incidents
tools.title: List active incidents
tools.description: Active (unresolved) incidents with their messages and affected components. GET /incident/list/active/{statuspage_id}.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Status.io reports no totals: ask for the next page until a page comes back empty.

tools.name: statusio_list_resolved_incidents
tools.title: List resolved incidents
tools.description: Resolved incidents (history) with their messages and affected components. GET /incident/list/resolved/{statuspage_id}.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Status.io reports no totals: ask for the next page until a page comes back empty.

tools.name: statusio_get_incident
tools.title: Get incident
tools.description: One incident in full: components, containers, infrastructure affected and all its messages. GET /incident/{statuspage_id}/{incident_id}.

incident_id.description: Incident id (from statusio_list_incidents or the active/resolved lists).

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

tools.name: statusio_get_incident_message
tools.title: Get incident message
tools.description: One message (update) of an incident: text, state, status, time and the user who posted it. GET /incident/message/{statuspage_id}/{message_id}.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

tools.name: statusio_list_maintenance_ids
tools.title: List maintenance ids
tools.description: The ids of all active, closed and upcoming maintenance events (ids only). Fetch one with statusio_get_maintenance. GET /maintenances/{statuspage_id}.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

tools.name: statusio_list_maintenance
tools.title: List maintenance
tools.description: Maintenance events in one state, with messages and affected components: pending (scheduled, not started), active (in progress) or closed (finished). GET /maintenance/list/{pending|active|closed}/{statuspage_id}.

state.description: pending = scheduled and not started, active = in progress, closed = finished.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Status.io reports no totals: ask for the next page until a page comes back empty.

tools.name: statusio_get_maintenance
tools.title: Get maintenance
tools.description: One maintenance event in full, with all messages and the infrastructure affected. GET /maintenance/{statuspage_id}/{maintenance_id}.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

tools.name: statusio_get_maintenance_message
tools.title: Get maintenance message
tools.description: One message of a maintenance event. GET /maintenance/message/{statuspage_id}/{message_id}.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

tools.name: statusio_list_subscribers
tools.title: List subscribers
tools.description: List the people and endpoints subscribed to the status page (email addresses, phone numbers, webhook hosts) with ids and their granular preferences. This is personal data of your subscribers. Webhook URLs are shortened to their host, because they can carry secrets. GET /subscriber/list/{statuspage_id}.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

tools.name: statusio_update_component_status
tools.title: Update component status
tools.description: WRITE: change the PUBLIC status of one component/container pair (for example to degraded_performance) without creating an incident. It changes what visitors of your status page see right away. Set it back to operational when done. Ids from statusio_list_components. POST /component/status/update.

container_id.description: Container id; it must be attached to that component.

details.description: Short message shown with the status change.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

tools.name: statusio_create_incident
tools.title: Create incident
tools.description: WRITE: open a new incident on the PUBLIC status page. It is visible to every visitor immediately and sets the status of the affected components. No subscriber, Slack, Teams, IRC or Twitter notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). Returns the new incident id. Say what is affected with all_infrastructure_affected or infrastructure_affected pairs. POST /incident/create.

all_infrastructure_affected.description: true = every component and container is affected. Otherwise give infrastructure_affected.

notify_email.description: Also email your email subscribers (default false).

notify_sms.description: Also text your SMS subscribers (default false).

notify_webhook.description: Also call your webhook subscribers (default false).

notify_slack.description: Also post to your connected Slack channels (default false).

notify_msteams.description: Also post to your connected Microsoft Teams channels (default false).

notify_irc.description: Also post to your connected IRC channel (default false).

post_to_twitter.description: Also post to your connected Twitter/X account (default false).

message_subject.description: Subject line for the email notification.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.

tools.name: statusio_update_incident
tools.title: Update incident
tools.description: WRITE: post a new update message on an existing incident and set its state and component status. The message is public at once. No subscriber or channel notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). To close an incident use statusio_resolve_incident. POST /incident/update.

status.description: Status the affected components get now.

notify_email.description: Also email your email subscribers (default false).

notify_sms.description: Also text your SMS subscribers (default false).

notify_webhook.description: Also call your webhook subscribers (default false).

tools.title: Resolve incident
tools.description: WRITE: resolve an incident with a closing message. The affected components return to operational and the incident moves to history. No notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). POST /incident/resolve.

tools.name: statusio_schedule_maintenance
tools.title: Schedule maintenance
tools.description: WRITE: schedule a planned maintenance on the PUBLIC status page. It is visible to visitors as upcoming maintenance. Subscribers are told only if you switch on notify_now / notify_72_hr / notify_24_hr / notify_1_hr (all default off). With automation true Status.io starts and ends it by itself at the planned times. Returns the maintenance id. POST /maintenance/schedule.

start.description: Planned start, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' (24-hour). Status.io's reference does not state the time zone of this input: check the scheduled time in your dashboard.

end.description: Planned end, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' (24-hour); after the start.

all_infrastructure_affected.description: true = every component and container is affected. Otherwise give infrastructure_affected.

notify_72_hr.description: Remind subscribers 72 hours before the start (default false).

notify_24_hr.description: Remind subscribers 24 hours before the start (default false).

notify_1_hr.description: Remind subscribers 1 hour before the start (default false).

automation.description: Start and end the maintenance automatically at the planned times (default false).

automation_start_text.description: Message posted when the maintenance starts (with automation).

automation_stop_text.description: Message posted when the maintenance ends (with automation).

message_subject.description: Subject line for the email notifications.

statuspage_id.description: Status page id. Defaults to the status page chosen when you connected.
